newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paribas sells stake in CMM Industries.
newsitem.headline: Paribas sells stake in CMM Industries.

text.p: French holding company Groupe Paribas and holding company Tisza said on Tuesday that Paribas was selling its controlling stake in CMM Industries to Tizsa for about 10 million francs, or 5.57 francs per share.
Tisza is acting with Siparex and Etienne Fouquet, who is chairman of Atos, 99.99 percent owned by CMM, the companies said.
Paribas is retaining its 444,642 convertible bonds in CMM issued in 1995.
After the sale, Tisza will control 63.2 percent of CMM, Siparex will hold 13.9 percent and Fouquet 11.9 percent.
Siparex, Tisza and Fouquet will make a public offer at a price of 5.60 francs per share for the remaining 222,981 shares of CMM.
The 1989 convertible bonds are reimbursable on January 1, 1997 and 1998, the 1995 convertible bonds are reimbursable on January 1, 1999.
The companies said holders of the bonds would be offered to convert those bonds in order to be able to take part in the offering.
The deal will allow Tisza to reinforce its activity of mechanical parts for the electrical industry and to offer CMM new possibilities for development, the companies said.
Tisza is a holding created in 1996 by the family company ESAC. Its only business is a 39 percent stake in ESAC of which Siparex holds 12 percent.
